method: TF-IDF full English stems and every option, word uni/bigrams, sublinear TF, cosine; scores retrieve candidates, never certify semantic distinctness. Public nearest is shown both with and without original target.
default_pool_basis: Read-only projection: committed stored selection IDs minus IDs in committed default-holds and nonlegacy-default-holds. Generated selection is not rewritten. This is not proof of deployment/publication or completed root QA.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has not sought an extension or other relief from the Board. Which continuing education plan satisfies the annual requirements?

choices.text: Five live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 15 home-study hours with no additional pharmacy-law content
Four live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 16 home-study hours
Six live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 14 home-study hours that include one hour of pharmacy law
Nine live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 10 home-study hours
Three live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 17 home-study hours

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A pharmacist has 13 eligible hours and finishes a 9-hour conference on a single day. Live, law, and specialized-topic requirements are satisfied.

How many conference hours may be applied under the stated daily CE limit? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 8 conference hours.
7 conference hours.
9 conference hours.
6 conference hours.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist who does not practice CDTM has 13 eligible CE contact hours. The pharmacist then completes 10 eligible hours at a conference on one calendar day. All live, law, and specialized-topic requirements are otherwise satisfied; the question concerns only the 20-hour total.

How many additional eligible contact hours are needed for that calendar year? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 7 contact hours
2 contact hours
1 contact hour
0 contact hours

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A pharmacist has completed 20 eligible CE contact hours for the year, including five live clinical hours and a two-hour ACPE-approved home-study course designated as pharmacy law. The law course addresses federal pharmacy requirements, not Massachusetts-specific rules. No specialized-practice requirement applies.

How should the law course be treated for the annual Massachusetts law-CE minimum? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Count it as general CE and add two hours specifically about Massachusetts law.
Count its two hours toward the law minimum as part of the 20-hour total.
Count it as general CE and repeat two law hours in a live format.
Count it toward the law minimum but exclude it from the general 20 hours.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy with a new prescription while the pharmacist on duty is counselling another patient. Which statements about who may take the call are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Only the pharmacist may take a new prescription by telephone.
Any pharmacy employee may take it and pass it to the pharmacist to check.
A pharmacy intern may receive a new prescription over the telephone.
An uncertified technician may take it provided the pharmacist verifies it afterwards.
A certified technician with the on-duty pharmacist's approval may receive it.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A technician's Massachusetts license remains active, but national certification expired yesterday. A new Schedule IV prescription is telephoned to the pharmacy.

Who should receive this new prescription under the personnel distinctions in the notes? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Route this new Schedule IV order to a recipient whose current scope permits it.
This technician, provided the call is described as a refill in the computer.
This technician, provided the pharmacist signs the entry before dispensing.
A trainee, provided the caller repeats the prescription to two employees.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A prescriber telephones a new Schedule VI prescription. The pharmacist on duty approves a Massachusetts-licensed technician with current national certification to receive the call. The prescriber supplies the drug, strength, directions, quantity, and other required information. No therapeutic clarification is needed.

Which workflow is consistent with the technician’s scope? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Route the call to the pharmacist because technician telephone authority is limited to unchanged refills.
Have the technician identify as certified and receive the order for pharmacist review.
Have the technician receive the order and complete its final dispensing verification.
Have the technician complete the clinical review because the prescriber supplied every required field.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts community pharmacist to administer methadone for addiction treatment. The patient presents a valid prescription from a practitioner, and the pharmacist has completed injection training and holds current CPR certification. May the pharmacist administer it there?

choices.text: Yes, because the pharmacist holds a valid prescription for the patient.
Yes, because the pharmacist has completed the required training and certification.
No, because that administration may occur only in a registered opioid treatment program.
No, because a pharmacist may never administer any medication for addiction treatment.
No, unless the prescriber attends the pharmacy at the time of administration.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A fully licensed technician has worked 520 hours after full licensure, has current CPR, and has completed the required six-hour vaccine course. National certification is not held. The documented on-the-job skills training has not yet occurred.

Which remaining requirement is identified by these facts? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Repeating 500 hours as a trainee before using the completed full-license hours.
Obtaining national certification because experience cannot be used instead.
Completing a PharmD before any supervised vaccine administration.
The additional documented on-the-job training and skills checklist.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
Case A: A technician completes a six-hour ACPE-accredited vaccination course that includes two live hours but skips the separate documented on-the-job training.

Case B: A second technician's course is entirely recorded video, and the pharmacy proposes substituting unsupervised practice for hands-on assessment.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Technician training may omit vaccine-reaction recognition if the pharmacist is present.
The six-hour course does not replace the additional two hours of documented on-the-job training.
The course must include the specified live instruction and hands-on technique assessment.
On-the-job training requires an experienced certified immunizer and documented skills assessment.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A technician's vaccine-training file contains a six-hour ACPE course completed entirely through recorded modules. The technician also completed two documented hours of on-the-job training with an experienced certified immunizer and a skills checklist. The MOR is reviewing the initial education requirements for the DPH vaccine program.

What education deficiency remains? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: None; the six course hours and two on-the-job hours may be combined into an undifferentiated eight-hour total.
The on-the-job hours must be doubled, after which the recorded course can count as the required live component.
The ACPE course must satisfy the live-training requirement; the additional on-the-job training does not replace it.
One hour of annual immunization CE can replace the missing course component because that is the pharmacist standard.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a prescription for generic buprenorphine sublingual tablets for opioid use disorder with a 90-day quantity. Which quantity rule should the pharmacist apply?

choices.text: A 30-day ceiling applies to every Schedule III opioid.
Every Schedule III prescription permits a 90-day fill.
The initial-opiate seven-day limit controls OUD treatment.
The OUD pathway may permit one fill of up to 90 days.
Five refills may be combined into one 90-day fill.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:

choices.text: The qualifying implantable-infusion-pump category.
An ordinary Schedule II opioid pain prescription solely because the patient has used it before.
A non-opioid Schedule II medication.
Buprenorphine prescribed for opioid use disorder.
Every Schedule III product regardless of treatment purpose or category.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A patient presents a valid oxycodone Schedule II prescription for 20 tablets and tells the pharmacist, before any dispensing, that she wants only 8 tablets because she is concerned about keeping extra opioid tablets at home. The pharmacy has all 20 tablets in stock. Which action is supported by Massachusetts law?

choices.text: Refuse the request because Schedule II prescriptions must be dispensed only in the exact quantity written.
Dispense all 20 tablets and advise the patient to discard the unwanted tablets at home.
Change the prescription quantity to 8 only after obtaining a replacement prescription from the prescriber.
Dispense the requested lesser quantity and document the partial dispensing in the patient record.
Treat the request as a pharmacy-stock shortage and use the federal 72-hour remainder rule.

What is the maximum quantity remaining under that 60-tablet authorization? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 20 tablets.
60 tablets.
15 tablets.
35 tablets.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A pharmacist discovers a dispensing error while the patient may still be exposed to harm. Which duties apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Immediately notify the patient or representative and give correction and harm-minimization directions.
Finish root-cause analysis before contacting the patient.
Always notify the patient before the prescriber in a strict sequence.
Immediately notify the prescriber when professional judgment indicates it is warranted.
Complete the initial QRE documentation within 24 hours after discovery or notification.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
Case A: A confirmed reportable breach of unsecured PHI affects 20 individuals, and the pharmacy proposes waiting until the annual HHS report to notify those individuals.

Case B: A manager treats the 60-day outer limit as an automatic permission to wait the full period even though earlier notice is feasible; no authorized delay applies.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The small-breach annual HHS route does not postpone the individual-notification obligation.
The small-breach HHS deadline is within 60 days after the discovery calendar year ends.
Notice must be provided without unreasonable delay, not routinely held until the outer limit.
One regulator filing necessarily serves as notice to all affected individuals.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A pharmacy discovers a confirmed controlled-substance theft. Its investigation will take several weeks. The manager proposes making no written contact with DEA until the completed electronic Form 106 is ready.

Which timeline correctly separates the two federal duties? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Notice: 45 days after discovery; Form 106: 1 business day after notice.
Notice: 1 business day; completed Form 106: 45 days after discovery.
Notice: 1 business day; completed Form 106: 45 days after investigation ends.
Notice and completed Form 106: both 45 days after discovery.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A community pharmacy receives by fax an otherwise valid Schedule II prescription for a routine ambulatory patient. The patient is not in an LTCF or hospice and the drug is not a qualifying narcotic compounded for direct parenteral or infusion use. May the fax itself serve as the original Schedule II prescription?

choices.text: Yes, every faxed Schedule II prescription is an original once a pharmacist receives it.
Yes, if the prescriber calls afterward to confirm the fax.
No; absent a federal fax-as-original exception, the fax does not itself replace the required original prescription.
No, because Schedule II prescriptions may never be transmitted by fax for any purpose.
Yes, if the quantity is a seven-day supply or less.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A Schedule II prescription is faxed for a resident of a qualifying long-term-care facility. The pharmacy has verified the required prescriber and patient information; other applicable requirements are satisfied.

What is the federal effect of the LTCF fax exception? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The fax is valid only as a follow-up to a previous emergency dispensing.
The fax permits release only if an emergency oral order is also obtained.
Treat this qualifying LTCF fax as the original, subject to the other requirements.
The fax permits preparation, but a paper original is required before release.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives several prescriptions for testosterone cypionate. Which scenarios fit the current statutory pharmacist-administration category specifically because of the indication? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A veterinarian's testosterone order for an animal, relying on the human gender-affirming administration provision
A prescribed dose for gender-affirming care
A subsequent prescribed gender-affirming dose after the pharmacist verifies the same authorized pathway remains satisfied
A prescribed dose for routine testosterone-replacement therapy for hypogonadism, relying only on the gender-affirming statute
A bodybuilding request with no valid prescription

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
Case A: For an eligible protected-care Schedule VI prescription, the prescriber requests the permitted practice-name label treatment.

Case B: Staff apply the same Schedule VI exception to testosterone and delete the actual prescriber identity from the pharmacy's original record.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Using a practice name means prescriber-identity verification is no longer necessary.
The eligible Schedule VI request must be assessed under the specific practice-name label pathway.
The Schedule VI label exception authorizes both the testosterone label change and erasure of internal prescriber identity.
Use in gender-affirming care makes every medicine Schedule VI.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A pharmacy's original controlled prescription contains the prescriber's DEA number. During label review, a technician assumes that every field on the original prescription must appear identically on the patient's container.

Which distinction should the pharmacist explain? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Information present in the original prescription need not be accurate on the label.
A correctly printed container label eliminates the need to retain the prescription.
Check the separate original-prescription, dispensing-record and label requirements.
The pharmacy can remove patient directions if the prescriber gives written instructions elsewhere.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: On Friday morning, a pharmacy discovers a significant unexplained loss of controlled substances. The investigation cannot be completed that day. Which federal response is correct?

choices.text: Wait for the investigation before contacting DEA.
Give oral notice within 24 hours and take no further action.
File Form 106 within one business day instead of separate notice.
Send written DEA notice within one business day and Form 106 within 45 calendar days.
Notify only the Massachusetts Board because the loss occurred in Massachusetts.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
Case A: A pharmacy discovers a reportable theft and plans to withhold the initial written DEA notice until a final quantity investigation is complete.

Case B: Staff confuse the current provision's completed electronic Form 106 period with the separate initial-notice deadline.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The retrieved current 21 CFR 1301.76(b) states 45 days after discovery for the complete electronic Form 106.
Significance depends on the specified circumstances and patterns rather than one universal dollar threshold.
The applicable initial written DEA notice is due within one business day of discovery.
A confirmed theft needs no report whenever only a small quantity was taken.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:

Case B: Staff confuse the current provision's completed electronic Form 106 period with the separate initial-notice deadline.

choices.text: Only losses above a universal fixed dollar threshold can be significant under the described rule.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem: A pharmacy refrigerator is found at 68°F after an overnight equipment failure. Several unopened insulin glargine cartons were stored there, and the pharmacy cannot yet determine how long the temperature was outside the labeled storage range. What should the pharmacist do with those cartons before dispensing?

choices.text: Dispense them normally because unopened prescription stock cannot be adulterated until it reaches a patient.
Relabel each carton with the observed temperature and dispense if the patient accepts the excursion.
Segregate the cartons from saleable stock and resolve product integrity under the labeling/manufacturer information before dispensing.
Return the cartons to refrigeration for one hour; restoring temperature automatically restores legal saleability.
Convert the cartons to patient-return inventory and use the ordinary returned-drug resale rule.

full_stem_and_all_options.stem:
A reconstituted product has a short labeled in-use period. Its unopened manufacturer's expiration is months away, and the patient's prescription remains valid for the rest of the year.

Which conclusion follows? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Limit use of the prepared product to its applicable in-use period.
Refrigerating the product restarts its manufacturer's expiration.
The prescription's annual validity becomes the prepared product's BUD.
A refill authorization permits use after the product's in-use limit.
